text:
sam_sales: heads-up — FintechCorp asked for a pricing option they can pitch to customers: baseline reserved capacity + a small pool of "cushion" credits that automatically cover seasonal spikes. they want to know how that would be packaged and what the overage billing looks like. need product input by wed so sales can include in proposal. @anne_pm @leah_finance

anne_pm: thanks. quick clarifying Qs: 1) is this purely commercial (pricing/contract) ask or do they need console UI + API changes? 2) expected spike profile (burst frequency, duration, peak tokens)? 3) target effective per-token when cushion is used?

sam_sales: good Qs. FintechCorp says: baseline 10M tokens/month reserved; spikes 2–3x for 2 week periods, ~3 times/yr. they asked for a single line item in invoice showing "reserved + cushion" and a blended effective rate for customer communications. they prefer no new API surface if possible.

leah_finance: from accounting standpoint we can support a blended rate on invoices but need clear rules for revenue recognition. cushion credits that are prepaid vs on-demand overage changes recognition timing. also need clear contract language for cushion replenishment and refunds.

diego_eng: technical constraints: runtime supports differentiation between reserved instances and burst routing, but auto-applying a prepaid cushion requires tagging requests with cushion_id or routing policy. we can implement server-side metering and a console toggle, but it's nontrivial — estimate 2 sprints if we need a UI + metering events. if we keep it as a billing-only construct (no API changes) we can fake it by post-hoc reconciliation but that complicates SLAs.

ops_support: we have an open support thread from FintechCorp with logs showing two recent spikes; attaching context here. they care about predictable latency during spikes — cannot accept throttling that increases 95p latency beyond 300ms.

billing-bot: Snapshot: FintechCorp current baseline usage = 9.4M tokens/mo. recent peak day = +180% token throughput. Last 30d avg token rate = 0.35 tokens/sec/req.

anne_pm: proposal draft: "Seasonal Cushion" package = reserved capacity X + prepaid cushion credits Y. Acceptance criteria before GA: (a) clear invoice line & contract wording, (b) backend metering to attribute cushion consumption, (c) console reporting for usage vs cushion, (d) fallback policy when cushion exhausted (auto-burst vs deny), (e) SLA impact doc.

leah_finance: +1 on those criteria. also require pricing ladder: e.g., cushion used <=20% of reserved -> blended rate A; 20–50% -> blended rate B; >50% -> surcharge C. need examples for legal.

sam_sales: customer also wants a simple example to share: "Reserve 10M + 2M cushion yields effective rate $X/token during cushion use" — they asked us to provide that number by Wed.

diego_eng: I can produce a defensible cost estimate quickly if finance gives the target margin. we need to know whether cushion is priced at reserved rate, discounted, or premium. current infra cost model: reserved tokens cost ~0.4x hosted per-token because of steady-state packing; burst is full cost.

anne_pm: decision points for product: (1) billing-only (fast, lower engineering scope) vs integrated (metering + UI, higher scope) (2) pricing model: discounted cushion vs premium overage (3) SLA changes and legal templating. My recommendation: ship billing-only pilot first for strategic accounts, gated by acceptance criteria (no SLA change for pilot).

leah_finance: pilot OK if prepaid cushion only (revenue recognized later) and pilot contracts clearly state no SLA uplift. finance to sign off on invoicing template.

ops_support: confirm we can route burst traffic to existing public pool for pilot. if yes, we can accept pilot but must monitor 95p latency. create monitoring dashboard and set alert thresholds.

sam_sales: sounds good — can we commit to a one-pager for the customer by Wed with two options: Billing-Only Pilot (fast) and Fully Integrated (longer timeline + SLA)?

anne_pm: yes. i'll draft one-pager with scope, timelines, and acceptance criteria. will include cost calc examples. action items: anne to create product intake ticket + attach sample invoice language; diego to size engineering effort for integrated option; leah to prepare pricing tiers and accounting notes; ops to create dashboard.

diego_eng: ETA for sizing: 5 working days. if we go billing-only pilot, engineering involvement = low (metering via logs + billing reconciliation) -> 3 days ops work.

leah_finance: I'll post sample tier table here once ready. quick ask: what's our threshold for "escalate to enterprise legal"? if customer asks for refund clauses on cushion, we escalate.

anne_pm: escalate if annual contract > $150k or if request changes revenue recognition (refunds, consumption-based credits).

sam_sales: noted. i'll update FintechCorp that we can provide a draft one-pager for Wed and propose a billing-only pilot unless they require SLA changes. will post customer acceptance after sync. :thumbsup: 

anne_pm: OK creating intake ticket now and will tag relevant owners. Ticket fields: customer, baseline, cushion size, pilot vs integrated, ARR impact, acceptance criteria, owner, target date.

billing-bot: Created ticket PRD-4837 assigned to anne_pm.

sam_sales: thanks — will add the customer email thread to PRD-4837.

anne_pm: closing loop — next steps captured in ticket. if anything changes ping here.

sam_sales: great, thanks all.
